title: The 1948 War

names.name: al-Nakba ("the catastrophe")
names.usage: name used by Palestinians and in the Arab world

summary: The war was fought in British-ruled Mandatory Palestine. On 29 November 1947 the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, a plan to divide the territory into Jewish and Arab states, and the next day fighting began as a civil war between the Jewish and Arab communities. On 14 May 1948 Israel declared independence, and the armies of neighbouring Arab states entered. Fighting, interrupted by UN-brokered truces, went on into 1949 and ended with separate armistice agreements between Israel and Egypt, Lebanon, Transjordan and Syria. Israel ended the war holding about 78% of the former mandate, more than the UN plan had given the Jewish state; Transjordan held the West Bank and Egypt the Gaza Strip. More than 700,000 Palestinians, over half of the Palestinian population, fled or were expelled. Palestinians call this mass displacement and dispossession the Nakba.

layers.title: UN partition plan (Resolution 181)
layers.note: The plan the UN General Assembly adopted on 29 November 1947: an Arab state and a Jewish state, each in three parts that meet at two crossing points, an Arab enclave at Jaffa, and Jerusalem with Bethlehem as an international zone run by the UN. It was never carried out. Its shading is shown until the first truce (11 June 1948), when the “Who held what” layer takes over; its boundary lines stay on the map for the whole war so the plan can be compared with what followed. Traced for this site by Claude (an AI) from the UN's own map of the plan (Map No. 103, November 1947), fitted to real coordinates using the map's printed latitude and longitude lines, and checked against the boundary description in the resolution. That map is small-scale (about 1:1,000,000) and its boundary lines are printed several hundred metres wide, so expect errors of a few hundred metres, up to about a kilometre in places. For example, the text puts Motza inside the Jerusalem zone, but the traced line leaves it about 700 m outside, and Qalqilya, which the text leaves in the Arab state, falls a few hundred metres on the Jewish side. The short stretch across the Dead Sea east of Ein Gedi is not drawn on the map; it follows the text ("due east to join the Transjordan frontier").

layers.title: Who held what (approximate)
layers.note: Roughly who held the ground at each stage of the war, so you can watch the front lines move. The map changes in steps, on the dates the main operations ended, not day by day. The first stages are traced from declassified CIA maps of the military situation on 11 June 1948 (the first truce) and 18 July 1948 (the second truce). For western Galilee we follow the July map, which puts its hills on the Arab side during the first truce, although the June map calls them “Jewish controlled”. The end state is the Israeli side of the 1949 armistice lines. The steps in between are our own estimate: the ground that changed hands after July is split into pieces, each dated by the operation that took it (see this topic’s events, and the sources below for Ha-Har, Beit Jibrin, al-Dawayima and Majdal). The Triangle villages are shown passing to Israel on the date of the armistice with Transjordan (3 April 1949), which moved them to Israel’s side; they were handed over in the weeks after. The pieces’ edges are rough, and the southern Negev is left unshaded until March 1949 because neither side held that largely empty desert. Expect errors of a kilometre or more. Ground Israeli forces held outside the former Mandate, in Lebanon (October 1948 to March 1949) and Sinai (December 1948 to January 1949), is not shown.

layers.title: 1949 armistice lines
layers.note: The lines that ended the fighting were agreed front by front: with Egypt on 24 February, Lebanon on 23 March, Transjordan on 3 April and Syria on 20 July 1949. They are drawn here as the lines that then held until 1967, and are shown from the first agreement onward, so fronts not yet settled appear early. The geometry is community-traced and not yet checked against the agreements' maps.
